stem: What common clinical finding might indicate a mandibular fracture during an intraoral examination?

options.text: Excessive flow of saliva from the parotid duct
A tear in the mucosa and bleeding near a tooth
The presence of rugae on the anterior palate
A yellow cigar-shaped object in the submandibular duct

explanation: Tears in the soft tissue mucosa, especially near the canine or posterior teeth, often accompany a break in the underlying bone.
rationale: Think about what happens to the skin of the teeth when the bone beneath it breaks.

optionExplanations.A: Saliva flow is a sign of healthy gland function and does not typically indicate skeletal trauma.
optionExplanations.B: Tears in the soft tissue mucosa, especially near the canine or posterior teeth, often accompany a break in the underlying bone.
optionExplanations.C: Rugae are normal anatomical landmarks on the roof of the mouth and are not related to trauma.
optionExplanations.D: This describes a salivary stone (sialolith), not a fracture.

originalCorrectOptionTexts: A tear in the mucosa and bleeding near a tooth
